newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa preparing team to help Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa preparing team to help Kabila's Congo.

text.p: The South African government is putting together a multi-disciplinary team to advise Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of Congo on reconstruction, but no date has been set for the initial fact-finding mission.

Deputy President Thabo Mbeki told a news conference on Thursday the team would leave within days, but a foreign ministry official said the Congo had asked in a letter that the visit should not take place before the end of June.

"We have an agreement with the government (of the Congo) to discuss with them a variety of matters that impact on the socio-economic situation there," Mbeki told reporters at the launch of a U.N. Development Programme report on poverty.

"So we'll be sending a delegation in the next few days to Kinshasa. They requested that we compose a delegation which would include for instance the (central) Reserve Bank, the economic ministries, people dealing with infrastructure, people who deal with public administration, and so on," Mbeki said.

The economy and industrial infrastructure of the former Zaire, potentially one of the richest countries in Africa, was left in tatters when former president Mobutu Sese Seko fled in May after 32 years of autocratic rule.

South Africa helped to broker a peaceful transfer of power from Mobutu to Kabila and has offered advice on reconstruction, but officials said on Thursday the finance and equipment would have to come from the international community.

Reserve Bank economic adviser Ernie van der Merwe told Reuters the central bank was on standby to send someone to the former Zaire to advise the new government on ways to rebuild the shattered fiscal infrastructure.
"It will be a fact-finding mission to determine what kind of assistance they need, to assess the problem," he said.
The Finance Ministry is ready to appoint a delegate to the team, but had not yet been told when the visit would take place, a spokeswoman said.
A government official said Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo discussed Kinshasa's needs Congo Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha at the recent Organisation of African Unity summit in Harare.
Karaha had since written to Pretoria listing areas on which Kinshasa would like South African advice. These included administration, infrastructure, transport and mining.
A transport ministry official told Reuters that no one had yet been delegated to the team, which will be led by Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad and will include private sector representatives.
Tom Tweedy, spokesman for De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd., said the diamond mining and marketing group was willing to join the team, but had not yet been asked.

"We are aware that a visit is being planned towards the end of the month by a delegation of representatives of South African industry to discuss possible involvement in rebuilding the economy of the Democratic Republic of Congo," he said.
An Anglo American Corporation spokeswoman said the gold mining group also hoped to be included in the delegation, but had not yet been asked.
De Beers, which controls the world diamond market through the London-based Central Selling Organisation, has a buying office in Kabila's Congo.

Anglo-American lost a tender for a copper/cobalt tailings project to American Mineral Fields Inc in April, but has a tender outstanding for a copper/cobalt project in Ruashi-Etoile, near the mining capital of Lubumbashi.
